title: CFP Committee Reveals 2026 Fourth Top‑25 Rankings and Bracket Shifts: Who’s Moving Up?
body:
The College Football Playoff (CFP) committee unveiled its fourth weekly ranking on Tuesday, confirming the University of Georgia Bulldogs as the nation’s top‑seeded team for the 2026 season. With the Bulldogs solidifying their No. 1 spot for the third consecutive week, the latest top‑25 list reshaped the playoff picture, elevated several surprise contenders, and set the stage for a dramatic run‑in to the postseason.

Georgia’s hold on the summit reflects a blend of dominant defense, efficient offense, and a schedule that has left few doubts about its superiority. Quarterback Stetson “Boom” McAllister, now a junior, has thrown for 2,845 yards and 28 touchdowns while limiting interceptions to just two, while the defensive line, anchored by senior defensive end Jalen “The Hammer” Rhodes, has recorded 13 sacks and forced eight turnovers in the past three weeks. The Bulldogs’ 10‑0 record, highlighted by a 38‑14 victory over No. 3 Ohio State and a defensive shutout of LSU, underscores why the committee has kept them perched at the apex of the rankings.

Trailing Georgia by a single spot is the Michigan Wolverines, who reclaimed the No. 2 slot after a convincing 31‑10 win over Purdue. The Wolverines’ resurgence hinges on a balanced attack that combines a revitalized ground game—running back Malik “Turbo” Johnson eclipsed 1,200 rushing yards this season—with a passing offense that has become more aggressive under new offensive coordinator Luis Alvarez. Michigan’s ascent also benefits from a relatively unblemished conference record, positioning them as the primary challenger to Georgia’s bid for a third straight national title.

The biggest surprise of the week is the elevation of the Boise State Broncos into the top‑10 at No. 9, propelled by a string of high‑scoring victories against Power Five opponents. Boise State’s spread‑offense wizardry, orchestrated by third‑year head coach Dana Whitaker, has produced an average of 45 points per game, while the defense has tightened, allowing just 17 points per contest over the last four weeks. Their climb illustrates the committee’s willingness to reward teams that dominate across both sides of the ball, even when they hail from a Group of Five conference.

Meanwhile, traditional powerhouses such as Alabama and Oklahoma found themselves slipping out of the top‑15, a stark contrast to their usual placement in the upper echelon. Alabama, now sitting at No. 18, suffered a narrow 27‑24 loss to Tennessee, exposing vulnerabilities in a secondary that has struggled against dual‑receiver sets. Oklahoma, at No. 16, has been hampered by injuries to its starting quarterback and a porous defensive front that has allowed an average of 34 points per game. Their descent signals a potential reshuffling of the conference hierarchies and opens the door for other SEC and Big 12 teams to make a push for playoff relevance.

The committee’s latest bracket also highlights the narrowing margin between the top four and the rest of the field. With the No. 4 slot occupied by the Clemson Tigers—who clinched the spot after a dramatic overtime win against Florida State—the race for the final playoff berth is intensifying. Clemson’s defense, led by sophomore linebacker Isaiah “The Wall” Monroe, has forced 22 turnovers in the past six games, a statistic that could prove decisive as the season reaches its climax. The Tigers sit just two wins away from securing a berth, but a slip could see them overtaken by emerging contenders such as the Texas Longhorns, who sit at No. 7 after a dominant 45‑21 victory over Baylor.

Looking ahead, the rankings set the tone for the final stretch of the regular season, where every conference championship game will carry amplified significance. Georgia will aim to preserve its unbeaten record against a formidable SEC rival, while Michigan seeks to cement its No. 2 position with a win over Ohio State in the Big Ten title game. Boise State’s meteoric rise will be tested against a Pac‑12 powerhouse, and Clemson must maintain its defensive intensity to stay in the playoff conversation. As the CFP committee prepares its final rankings in early December, the current top‑25 snapshot underscores a season marked by both continuity at the summit and volatility among the challengers, promising an exhilarating road to the 2026 national championship.
